solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Holiday cheese includes opening for sandwich

definitions.note: a festa is an Italian festival or holiday

indicators.note: the cheese word holds the next piece inside it
the opening of a word is its first letter, so only the first of sandwich is used

explanation.surface: A holiday treat: cheese with a bit of sandwich tucked in.
explanation.definitionFit: Festa is the Italian word for a feast day, used in English for a festival or holiday.

clue.text: Distinctive character including meeting with no act before anger — quite the opposite (11, two words)

indicators.note: the first part comes before the word for anger in the answer
the aura word takes the shortened meeting inside it

parts.note: an aura is the distinctive air or character about someone

indicators.note: the word for meeting is used without the letters of act

parts.note: a contact is a meeting or touching

explanation.surface: Someone describes a character who meets others without acting first, and the reply is that it is the reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase is used in English to mean 'on the contrary', flatly contradicting what was said.

clue.text: Scalp disease? Iris's head has present involving it

indicators.note: the first letter of the surname gets the word for present wrapped round it

parts.note: Iris Origo was an Anglo-Italian biographer

explanation.surface: Asking whether a woman's head has a scalp complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: PR, a dictionary abbreviation for present, goes round O, the head of ORIGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Porrigo is an old medical term for scaly eruptions of the scalp such as ringworm.

clue.text: What may have been wielded by shipmen, right? (9, two words)

definitions.text: What may have been wielded by shipmen, right?

indicators.note: wielding handles something with force, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A question about what sailors might have brandished.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: sailors could well wield such a net, and the letters of shipmen plus RT make it.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrimp net is a hand net on a pole for catching shrimps, the kind of gear seamen could use.

clue.text: Source of peat is removed from Jock's dish

indicators.note: the two letters of is are taken out of the Scottish dish

parts.note: Jock is a nickname for a Scot, and haggis is the Scottish national dish

explanation.surface: Something is taken out of a Scotsman's dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' reads as a plain verb after 'peat', but it is the pair of letters taken away from the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A hagg is a Scots term for a broken piece of moss ground or bog, from which peat is cut.

clue.text: Former record as retained in what's left

indicators.note: the short piece is kept inside the remainder word

parts.note: e.g. means 'for example', which can stand for 'as' (as in 'such as')

explanation.surface: An old record survives in whatever remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Regest is an archaic word for a register or written record.

clue.text: Long time I'll be held in fellow's grasp — Lydia's alter ego?

definitions.note: noun: a Maeonian is a person of Maeonia, i.e. a Lydian

indicators.note: the long time and I sit inside the word for fellow
the fellow's grasp is what encloses the other letters

parts.note: an aeon is an immensely long age

explanation.surface: Someone waits a long time clasped in a man's arms, with a mystery about a woman's other self.
explanation.walkthrough: Lydia looks like a woman's name, but it is the ancient country in Asia Minor, whose older name was Maeonia.
explanation.definitionFit: Maeonia was the old name for Lydia, so a Maeonian is another name for a Lydian; Homer was sometimes called the Maeonian.

clue.text: Prince you'd left restyled in stately fashion

indicators.note: giving something a new style rearranges it, so these letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A prince has left after being given a new look, and carries it off grandly.
explanation.definitionFit: Proudly can mean in a grand, imposing or majestic manner, as a stately building stands.

clue.text: What's a bit like roti — two halves thereof go for a little local cash

definitions.note: noun phrase: the answer is another Indian flatbread

indicators.note: swapping the two halves of the answer gives the coin; equivalently the coin's halves change places

parts.note: an anna was a small coin of India, a sixteenth of a rupee

explanation.surface: An Indian bread is broken in two and the halves are swapped for small change.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: swap the answer's halves and you get the coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Naan and roti are both flatbreads of South Asian cooking, so one is quite like the other.

clue.text: Number in sets once forming holy place

indicators.note: the number abbreviation goes inside the old word for sets

parts.note: teme is an obsolete word for a team or set

explanation.surface: Groups of people in the past made up a sacred site.
explanation.definitionFit: A temenos is the sacred precinct round a Greek temple, land set apart for a god.

clue.text: Dandy/rake, right to left, neither first, in Gregorian cadence

indicators.note: neither first means neither word keeps its first letter, so both opening letters go
right to left tells us to read the two words backwards

parts.note: a beau is a dandy, a fop
a roué is a rake, a debauchee

explanation.surface: A list of foppish men followed by a churchy musical term, set out like a puzzle note.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading BEAU/ROUE backwards gives EUORUAEB; the first letters of the two words, R and B, drop out.
explanation.definitionFit: Euouae is the vowel string of 'seculorum Amen' used to mark the closing cadence of a psalm tone in plainchant.

clue.text: Procession, notice, in trim

indicators.note: the notice goes inside the trim word

explanation.surface: A notice about a procession is put in neat order.
explanation.definitionFit: A parade is a ceremonial procession or march past.

clue.text: Pouring process, i.e. translation of ode in including most of choral work

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap round the shortened choral work
translating something turns it into new form, so these letters are rearranged
the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a cantata is a work for choir and voices

explanation.surface: A translated ode is put into a choral piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Decantation is the act of pouring liquid gently off its sediment, as with wine.

clue.text: See wanton opening fantastic legs to writhe

indicators.note: the jumbled legs are opened up to take the other letters inside
fantastic means wildly fanciful, so the letters of legs are rearranged

parts.note: C stands for see in the blog's reading, a dictionary abbreviation
a rig is an old word for a wanton woman

explanation.surface: Watch a wanton display fantastic legs and wriggle.
explanation.definitionFit: Scriggle is a dialect word meaning to wriggle or squirm.

clue.text: Driver avoiding circling the majority of ridges

indicators.note: the driver word avoids, i.e. drops, the letters of most, here the closing pair
most circles the answer inside the driver word, so its opening pair is dropped as well

explanation.surface: A motorist steers clear of going round most ridges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The majority' is MOST, which sits as MO...ST round the answer inside MOTORIST; avoid it and the ridges are left.
explanation.definitionFit: Tori, plural of torus, are rounded convex mouldings or ridges, in architecture and anatomy.

clue.text: Declare singular turns relation left out

indicators.note: the singular word is turned round
the letter for left is dropped

explanation.surface: A single object turns and a relative is excluded.
explanation.definitionFit: To enounce is to state or pronounce formally, i.e. to announce.

clue.text: A copycat turns revealing personality's innermost part

indicators.note: the whole is read backwards

parts.note: the mina or myna is a bird famous for mimicking speech

explanation.surface: A mimic changes course, showing who they are deep down.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jungian psychology the anima is the inner self or soul, the innermost part of the psyche.

clue.text: Eccentric baron, being ill and dysfunctional

indicators.note: an eccentric is off-centre, so the letters of baron are disordered

parts.note: mal is French and old English for bad or ill

explanation.surface: A peculiar nobleman who is sick and not working right.
explanation.definitionFit: Abnormal means departing from the usual, which dysfunctional also describes.

clue.text: Fairy or tube worm? Not so

indicators.note: 'Not so' says that so is not there, so its two letters are dropped from the worm

parts.note: the sand mason is a marine worm that builds a tube of sand grains

explanation.surface: Asking whether something is a fairy or a worm that lives in a tube, and the answer is no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not so' looks like a reply, but it means remove the letters of so.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sandman is a folklore figure who sprinkles sand to bring children sleep, a sort of sprite.

clue.text: Big mat's adjusted for viola player

indicators.note: adjusting rearranges, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A large mat is straightened out for a string player.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambist plays the viola da gamba, a bowed string instrument held between the legs.

clue.text: What kids model with fell round messy pit

indicators.note: the dreadful word goes round the other letters

parts.note: fell as an adjective means fierce or dreadful, like dire

indicators.note: a mess is disorder, so the letters of pit are jumbled

explanation.surface: Children make something with whatever fell around a muddy hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell' looks like a verb, but it is the old adjective meaning cruel or terrible.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirt pie is a mud pie, the shape children mould from wet earth.

clue.text: Oilman abroad in foreign city

indicators.note: abroad can mean astray or widely scattered, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: An oil executive is working overseas in a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Milano is the Italian name for Milan, a city foreign to English speakers.

clue.text: Veg sewn in recess, calm

indicators.note: the vegetable is stitched inside the recess

parts.note: an apse is a vaulted recess in a church

explanation.surface: Vegetables are stitched into an alcove, then all is quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: To appease is to pacify or soothe someone, making them calm.

clue.text: 'Salve', following a R, i.e. 'scare off '

indicators.note: the salve word comes after the other letters

parts.note: oint is an old verb meaning to anoint or apply salve

explanation.surface: A quotation game of words after the letters A and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Aroint is Shakespeare's command to be gone ('Aroint thee, witch'), driving someone away.

clue.text: Chaps holding assistant up in the middle

indicators.note: the men word holds the other inside
in a down clue, up means the word is read bottom to top

explanation.surface: Men raise a helper so she is in the centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Median as an adjective means situated in the middle, as in a median line.

clue.text: Nautical cord e.g. twisted with open arm

indicators.note: twisting a cord is like twisting letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A ship's rope, for instance, is wound round an outstretched arm.
explanation.definitionFit: A manrope is a rope on a ship's side used as a handrail when going up or down.

clue.text: Tipples one bottled? These ones are different (from E. India)

definitions.text: These ones are different (from E. India)
definitions.note: plural noun: nipa is also an alcoholic drink made from palm sap in the East Indies

indicators.note: the one is kept inside like liquor in a bottle

explanation.surface: A drink is bottled up, with a hint that East Indian drinks differ.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the wordplay: these are not small tots of spirit but palm-sap drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Nipa is an East Indian palm and the alcoholic beverage brewed from its sap.

clue.text: Names in blue for laxative drug

indicators.note: the names abbreviation sits inside the blue word

parts.note: the blue is a poetic name for the sea
nn. is the plural abbreviation of n., name, as n. is doubled for plurals like pp. for pages

explanation.surface: Names are written in blue ink for a laxative prescription.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Names in' looks like anagram fodder, but blue here is the sea and names is NN.
explanation.definitionFit: Senna is a purgative made from the dried leaves or pods of cassia plants.

clue.text: Stir uneasily in plot of a brownish hue

indicators.note: the mixed letters go inside the plot word

parts.note: a flower bed is a plot

indicators.note: uneasiness is restlessness, so the letters move around

explanation.surface: Someone shifts uneasily in a flower bed of brown colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Bistre is a brown pigment from soot, so bistred means tinted with that brown.

clue.text: Runs short of century causing grief

definitions.note: adjective: sore can mean distressing or painful

indicators.note: the score is missing the letter for century

parts.note: in cricket, a batsman's score is his runs

explanation.surface: A batsman falling short of a hundred is upsetting.
explanation.definitionFit: Sore in older use means grievous or painful, as in a sore loss.

clue.text: Once in Scotland forebear becomes free of stress

indicators.note: the word for stress is removed

parts.note: an ancestress is a female forebear

explanation.surface: A forebear finds relief from strain.
explanation.definitionFit: Ance is the Scots form of once, so it has the same sense of one time or formerly.

clue.text: Measure luminous appearance, not gold

indicators.note: the gold letters are removed

parts.note: a meteor is a bright streak in the sky
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Gauging a bright glow that turns out not to be gold.
explanation.definitionFit: To mete is to measure out or allot, as in to mete out punishment.

clue.text: Run isn't common in the sea

indicators.note: the vulgar word sits inside the sea word

parts.note: the main is the open sea
ain't is common, i.e. vulgar, for isn't

explanation.surface: A shipping route is not shared in the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain a business is to keep it going, much as one would run it.

clue.text: Story going about in Israel

indicators.note: going about suggests moving around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tale circulating in the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: A serial is a story published or broadcast in instalments.

clue.text: Behaves in accordance with son in stuffed jacket (6, two words)

indicators.note: the son letter goes inside the jacket

parts.note: an acton was a quilted jacket worn under armour

explanation.surface: Someone does what they are told while a boy is inside a padded coat.
explanation.definitionFit: To act on advice is to behave as it directs, following it.

clue.text: Adolescent about staggerin', like the avenue?

indicators.note: the adolescent goes about the staggering word

parts.note: a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth
reelin' with the dropped g, as in casual speech

explanation.surface: A teenager is staggering about along a boulevard.
explanation.walkthrough: A Teddy boy was a 1950s British youth in Edwardian-style dress.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenue is classically a road lined on each side by trees, so it is bordered with them.
